image_description: A close-up, underwater shot of a hammerhead shark swimming towards the left. The shark's distinctive cephalofoil (hammer head) is prominent, with eyes at the tips. The body is greyish-blue on top and white underneath. In the background, there are blurry shapes of other fish and blue water. There is visible text overlay in the upper left corner.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the laterally expanded, dorsoventrally flattened cephalofoil (hammer-shaped head).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly displays the characteristic T-shaped head structure unique to hammerhead sharks.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are positioned at the extreme lateral tips of the cephalofoil.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The eye on the visible side is located at the very end of the lateral extension of the head.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Nostrils are positioned near the lateral margins of the cephalofoil.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The resolution and angle do not allow for clear visualization of the nostrils; they are likely present but not distinctly testable.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Anterior margin of the cephalofoil is straight to slightly curved with a central indentation in some species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The front edge of the hammer appears relatively straight/slightly curved, consistent with general hammerhead morphology.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is streamlined and laterally compressed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the torso shows a smooth, tapered shape typical of pelagic sharks.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Dorsal coloration is grey to brownish with white ventral surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The shark exhibits countershading: grey/blue on the dorsal side and white on the belly/underside.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is covered in dermal denticles with a rough texture.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Image resolution is insufficient to resolve individual dermal denticles; skin appears smooth due to distance/lighting.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: First dorsal fin is tall and falcate (sickle-shaped), positioned anteriorly.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The first dorsal fin is located further back on the body and is not visible in this close-up framing of the head and pectorals.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Pectoral fins are broad and triangular.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible pectoral fin is broad and has a triangular shape, matching the description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Caudal fin is asymmetrical with a pronounced upper lobe.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail (caudal fin) is completely out of frame.

artifact_observations.location: Upper left quadrant, floating in the water background
artifact_observations.reasoning: There is a cluster of characters that resemble text or a watermark but are illegible and nonsensical ('JDM...'). This is a common AI artifact where the model attempts to render text but fails to produce coherent letters.

The skin texture is overly smooth and plastic-like, lacking the subtle granularity or dermal denticle detail expected in a high-fidelity biological rendering, though this may be partly due to image compression.

artifact_observations.location: Right edge of the frame, behind the shark's head
artifact_observations.reasoning: There is an ambiguous brownish shape on the right edge that seems to merge indistinctly with the background or the shark's body, lacking clear definition.
